result.summary: I recounted seal 01 chk115 from the raw artifacts with my own parsers (C:/kyty/s115/audit115/recount/: recount_vid.py, recount_f2.py, myglitch.py, scan_boot.py, *.out.txt). check115.py was not imported. Every number the verdict rests on is CONFIRMED and the verdict PASS stands. vid115 has 3894 frames (ffprobe packets, decoded frames and the index agree) and 0 one-frame glitches: my own detector's nearest candidate has a neighbour ratio of 1.025, far above the 0.35 cut. I recomputed the stable frame as 466, which gives 3418 scene rows. UpdateTitle costs 31.297 us per call (row median 24.086), present_overlap is 0, there are no failure markers in the log or stdout, and the bda_scan median is 51. boot115a (10111 ms, 607/0) and boot115c (10115 ms, 606/0) both reach the scene. boot115b prints exactly one 'PrepareMainPresent: mode 1', then the :326 fatal after the PrepareHold line (log lines 4284, 4285, 4291), and has no wait line. All four pre_run gpu_util_median values are 2.0. Every setup condition holds: env, gates text identical to gates_base.txt with no titleasync, the pin, the hold, one attempt each, all binary_sha256 d3a981a2. All 18 seal hashes and the amendment hashes match; archive copies are byte-equal. The installed exe is d3a981a2. The build matches 7c73f26 source: PE link stamp 10:18:42 local, last src mtime 08:23:11, no non-docs diff 7c73f26..HEAD, and the embedded banner reads e68bb6e-dirty. The F2 figures in item 9 are CONFIRMED over n>=300 (3584 rows): median 2.429, p90 4.211, p99 5.761 nearest-rank, max 12.941 ms, flip_rsv_wait_n 0 on every row, no FlipHold lines, mt_age 88.4 us. The findings are all MINOR or INFO. Item 9 calls the n>=300 window 'scene frames', but 166 of its rows are before the stable frame. Its speed-track inputs cannot be reproduced exactly from any stated window, and its per-operation arithmetic comes to 6.2 us, not 6.3. The 'never waited' statement holds only within the scope; there were 3 waits at startup. Item 8 says the control died 'after the hold', but it died about 7.4 s after launch, inside the 10-s hold. A v4 acceptance stage ran on 2 workers throughout the chain and neither item 8 nor item 9 mentions it. Smaller points: the seal text says v2 while v3 was hashed and used; the refused chain installed the build and left it installed; the BDA regime has 8% full rescans; game-X range trivia.

result.summary:
Code-review lens, commits 503a8bf (presentation-ring fix) and 7c73f26 (titleasync default 1). No BLOCKER or MAJOR. At defaults the only callers of Presenter::Present and of PrepareBlankFrame without a producer are in the VideoOut present thread: videoOut.cpp:831, 843, 853-854, 871-872 and FlipQueue::Flip :1182, which only PresentThread calls. The only other call site is window.cpp:1007-1009, which runs only when KYTY_PREPARE_MAIN_PRESENT=1. Two related paths were checked and do not record into present_scheduler: the GuestGpu thread's PrepareFrame and PrepareBlankFrame(&buffer), which record into the GuestGpu buffer, and the screenshot/RenderDoc hooks, which run inside Present or Flip. So the present ring has one producer, and C1 (two threads in Present) is impossible by construction, as ROADMAP 115 items 1 and 8 claim (CONFIRMED). That rests on reading the code: nothing enforces it at run time.

The main thread no longer touches ImGui state during preparation. SetShaderPreparationOverlay only stores atomics, and ProcessEvent in the preparation loop only changes main-thread-only g_input_* globals. The ImGui context and Vulkan backend are now built and used by the present thread alone, which is an improvement over the old two-thread use.

End of preparation while the present thread is inside Present is harmless. The flag is read once at entry; PrepareFrame falls through to the IME path and draws nothing; at most one present is counted after the snapshot is taken.

Titles posted before the main loop are bounded at one queued task. title_queued stays true until the first DrainMainThreadTasks in Run, and each log shows exactly one startup MainTaskLate line.

With KYTY_PREPARE_HOLD_MS unset, a long cold preparation still shows the overlay. m_precache_active is set before the precache thread starts. The present path takes only the render mutex, queue_mutex and the frame pool. The precache thread takes only PipelineCache::m_mutex. So nothing links the two, but a real cold preparation was not run (the claim is already scoped to warm preparation with a 10 s hold).

At the default path, SDL_QUIT during preparation leads to quick_exit(0) with the present thread still running, the same situation as the normal exit.

Build provenance checks out. The installed exe, the pinned copy and the build output all have sha256 d3a981a23fc1c5df. The build label is e68bb6e-dirty. The binary's knob table reads titleasync fallback 1 limit 1, daslot 1, daguard 1, cspfree 1, bdanarrow 0.

Remaining issues:
- Stale comments that now state the opposite of the code (MINOR).
- No run-time enforcement of the one-thread claim (MINOR).
- On macOS, surface recreation during preparation stalls the overlay, because WindowPrepareShaders never drains main-thread tasks (MINOR).
- Several INFO notes: a torn overlay frame is possible at the end of preparation; the present thread is no longer parked before Run, which shifts KYTY_KEYS @present numbering and KYTY_REC indices by about 10 frames; item 9 draws its numbers from two different row windows.

Scratch scripts: C:/kyty/s115/audit115/code/scan_logs.py and C:/kyty/s115/audit115/code/recount_x.py.

findings.title: Comments left from session 114 now say the opposite of the new pre-loop behaviour
findings.evidence: src/graphics/presentation/window/windowInternal.h:76-78 still says that until Run() 'UpdateTitle keeps the waiting path, which parks the present thread while WindowPrepareShaders presents from the main thread'. After 503a8bf the pre-loop path always posts (window.cpp:1179 `title_async = !loop_running || ...`) and the main thread does not present. window.cpp:848 says 'from here on UpdateTitle may take the async title path', but now the knob decides from that point on. window.cpp:968-969 says KYTY_PREPARE_HOLD_MS 'keeps presenting the preparation screen from the main thread ... the stress for the startup park', but the hold now keeps the overlay active for the present thread and the park no longer exists. swapchain.cpp:843-845 explains the PresentOverlap zone by 'the startup park itself happens inside UpdateTitle'. gates.cpp titleasync row says 'Read on every UpdateTitle call', but it is now read only after the loop starts. None of these files or lines was touched by the patch (patch_s115a.py edits only the UpdateTitle comment block).
findings.fix: Update the five comments to the session-115 model: before Run, UpdateTitle always posts; the main thread only pumps SDL events; the hold keeps the overlay active for the VideoOut thread; there is no startup park; the knob is read only once main_loop_running is set. Do it in the next code commit so later audits do not reason from the old model.

findings.title: 'C1 closed by construction' is proven only by reading the code; no run-time check guards it
findings.evidence: The claim (ROADMAP 115 items 1 and 8) is correct today: the only non-PresentThread caller of Present/PrepareBlankFrame(nullptr) is window.cpp:1007-1009, behind KYTY_PREPARE_MAIN_PRESENT. The guards behind it are weak. The PresentOverlap detector (swapchain.cpp:846-867) only counts and logs up to 8 lines. The ring-owner EXIT (commandRecorder.cpp:326) fires only when RecordThreadWanted is true for the present scheduler; it is false with KYTY_GPU_CHECKPOINTS or GPU-time runs, as noted in session 101. In that mode a future second caller, or the positive control itself, would race in Present/ImGui/FramePool without any fatal signal. The permanent ROADMAP wording ('C1 закрыт по построению') does not say that it relies on this inspection.
findings.fix: Record in ROADMAP that the guarantee is by inspection of these call sites. Optionally make it enforced: remember the VideoOut PresentThread id at start, and in Presenter::Present and PrepareBlankFrame(producer==nullptr) EXIT on any other thread unless KYTY_PREPARE_MAIN_PRESENT=1. The positive control would then fail the same way whether or not the record thread is on.

findings.title: macOS: surface recreation during preparation now blocks the present thread until WindowRun, freezing the overlay
findings.evidence: swapchain.cpp:569-576: on __APPLE__, Swapchain::Recreate(surface_lost) calls m_window.RunOnMainThread(RecreateSurface). Before 503a8bf the main thread presented during preparation, so this ran inline (IsMainThread, window.cpp:773). Now only the present thread presents, and WindowPrepareShaders (window.cpp:988-1018) never calls DrainMainThreadTasks. A surface loss during preparation therefore parks the present thread in RunOnMainThread until Run() drains, and the preparation screen freezes for the rest of the preparation. It is not a deadlock: Run drains first. Windows is unaffected (RecreateSurface is called directly).
findings.fix: Call g_window->DrainMainThreadTasks() in the WindowPrepareShaders loop, next to SDL_PollEvent. The only pre-loop tasks are the coalesced title and surface recreation, both safe on the main thread. This also applies the startup title early.

findings.title: Possible one-frame torn preparation overlay at the end of preparation
findings.evidence: systemOverlay.cpp:479-483: SetShaderPreparationOverlay(false) uses the defaults completed=0, total=0. It stores total=0 (relaxed) before active=false. The present thread's PrepareFrame (:975, :994) can read active==true and then total==0, and draw 'Reading saved shaders...' instead of the full progress bar for the final frame. During updates, completed and total can also tear, which min() clamps. The window is a few instructions wide, so this is cosmetic.
findings.fix: When deactivating, store g_shader_preparation=false first (or keep the last counters). Alternatively, pack completed and total into one 64-bit atomic.

findings.title: Present thread no longer parked before Run: extra startup presents shift KYTY_KEYS @present and KYTY_REC numbering; startup MainTaskLate line persists
findings.evidence: rec_vid114.mp4.idx: 1 present, then a 0.232 s gap (the park), matching MainTaskLate us=229700. rec_vid115.mp4.idx: 11 presents in 0.150 s at about 60 Hz before the first gap (1.038 s at frame 11). Each non-preparing Present calls InputScript::Poll (m_presents++), records a KYTY_REC frame and calls UpdateTitle. So @<present> numbers and the KYTY_MAIN_STALL_TEST frame count now include about 10 extra startup presents compared with 114 builds, more with a long LoadElf. The pre-loop title task still ages until Run: MainTaskLate: us=471907 (vid115), 10341415 (boot115a), 10268377 (boot115c), which uses 1 of the 32 log lines and would satisfy a scorer that takes the maximum over MainTaskLate lines (the ctl114 b_main_slept pattern, audit 114 note (и)). FrameTrace mt_age_ns is not polluted (first rows 28-94 us).

findings.title: Only a warm preparation with a 10 s hold was tested; by code nothing ties the present path to a real cold preparation

For a real cold preparation, pipelineCache.cpp:6144 sets m_precache_active before the thread starts, so the loop does not exit early. The precache thread takes only PipelineCache::m_mutex (no GetMutex()/queue_mutex in pipelineCache.cpp). The present path takes the render mutex, queue_mutex and the frame pool. FinishPreparation (about 96 ms WriteDriverCache in boot115a) now runs while the overlay is still presented by the VideoOut thread, which is better than before. findings.title: SDL_QUIT/CLOSE during preparation: quick_exit runs while the present thread keeps presenting
findings.evidence: window.cpp:993-998 returns false, then emulator.cpp:187-188 calls std::quick_exit(0). at_quick_exit runs Subsystems::EmergencyShutdownActive (Log::Shutdown, FileSystem, Controller, SaveData). Graphics has no emergency hook, so the VideoOut present thread may still be inside vkQueuePresentKHR or LOGF while the log shuts down. Before 503a8bf the present thread was often parked at this point; now it presents at 60 Hz. This is the same class as the normal WindowRun exit path, so it is not a regression of the ring fix.
findings.fix: Optional: before quick_exit, request the VideoOut jthread stop, or make LOGF after Log::Shutdown a no-op.

result.reasoning:
I checked every part of the evidence myself and could not refute it. The factual core holds.

**The job (CONFIRMED)**
- small_v4.log shows '== ttl114b_subset [14:15:03]' through '== done [14:28:18]'.
- ttl114b_subset_w2.report.txt: work dir ttl114b_39992_1790338504. Epoch 1790338504 is 12:15:04 UTC, i.e. 14:15:04 local.
- BASELINE 181.2 s and BASELINE#2 181.8 s ran in parallel. Store: 193 files, 4 122.9 MB. Wall 794.8 s, worker time 1 572.4 s, 2 workers.
- The 12 jobs sum to 1 209.3 worker-seconds, packed into the roughly 609 s after the baselines (14:18:06 to 14:28:15). So both workers were busy almost continuously through the chain.
- This is a mutlib run on a real sealed suite: s114 ttl114b.py, 9 mutants plus 3 controls.

**The chain (CONFIRMED)**
- Main transcript: go115a relaunched at 12:19:48.375Z (14:19:48 local).
- go115a.log: vid115 started 14:20:22; boot115c ended 14:26:32; done 14:26:37.

**The builder agent (CONFIRMED)**
- agent-aa0c9be95b9dad5c3 meta: 10:20:51; last write 14:51:46.
- It ran 'bash small_v4.sh' at 12:10:24Z and polled the log from 12:20:38Z to 12:28:20Z.
- It was the only workflow agent alive during the chain.

**Amendment 1 was the enabler (CONFIRMED)**
- go115a_refused2.log: the 14:18:26 refusal was caused only by python 12940/36096 (the parallel baselines), then 13140/45036, each at about 1.0 CPU s/s.
- Between 14:18:33 and 14:19:02 the executor went straight from reading that log to writing the item-7 patch. It never checked the processes' command lines.
- Amendment 1 (14:19) names them 'two light self-check processes' and raises the gate to 1.5 per process / 4 total. The relaunch then passed with the same workers still running.

**Rules (wording CONFIRMED)**
- ROADMAP 114 item 6 lists mutlib and agents as heavy processes and forbids any of them in parallel with a sealed chain.
- CLAUDE.md says 'ни агентов, ни сборок, ни мутантов'.
- small_v4.sh's header says 'never during a sealed run'. mutlib.py:5559 refuses 'no parallel CPU work' too, but only at startup, as does small_v4.sh's step().
- Item 7's 'им разрешено работать всегда' is false against the builder prompt. That prompt allows at any time only py_compile, static checks and tiny synthetic triples with --workers 2.

**Nuances that weaken the finding**
1. The builder did not break its own prompt. Its heavy gate covers only 'more than 2 workers on a real suite', so a 2-worker real-suite run fell into a gap: neither gated nor in the allowed-any-time list. The root cause is that gap plus the executor's unchecked label.
2. Session 115 item 4 explicitly lets the v4 workflow's agents stay alive during sealed chains, with only heavy commands gated. So 'agent alive' alone is not a breach; the concurrent mutant run is.
3. Item 7 was recorded before the run, so the letter of 'decision before action' was kept. The decision rested on a false premise.
4. Minor: 'PIDs change every sample' is overstated. The first pair persisted across two samples; they were the two baselines.

**Impact on the seal verdict**
- The PASS is robust. The checks are one-sided (frames 3 894 ≥ 3 000; presents 607/606 ≥ 300).
- The boot115b control reproduced commandRecorder.cpp:326 under the same load, so the load did not mask the race.
- Item 9's F2 decision (zero waits) is one-sided in the safe direction.
- So no BLOCKER.

**My additional evidence that the load plausibly contaminated the levels**
- Scratch scripts are in C:/kyty/s115/audit115/p1_skeptic/ (cmp.py, cmp2.py, clk.py). Numbers are for FrameTrace n ≥ 400.
- vid115 against the same-scene videos:

| | vid114 (BDA OLD) | vtt114b | vid115 (BDA NEW) |
|---|---|---|---|
| dt mean | 32.1 ms | 33.0 ms | 35.4 ms |
| cpu_gpu_us mean | 31.2 ms | 32.1 ms | 34.3 ms |
| dt p90 | 35.5 ms | 36.3 ms | 48.2 ms |
| frames > 40 ms | 3.0 % | 6.1 % | 15.1 % |
| video frames | 4 010 | — | 3 894 |

- vid115 was the worse run even though OLD is the slower regime and vid114 ran in OLD. GPU SM clocks were equal or higher (medians 2 332 / 2 325 / 2 377 MHz).
